name: blast-drill-plan-ui
description: Visual verification of drill plan UI: grid creation, hole markers, camera orbit, replace grid

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:4 spacing:5 depth:6 start:12,12
steps.description: The grid tool's spacing stepper defaults to 3m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts) — dragging this rectangle at that default would compute a different rows/cols than this command declares (round(15/3)+1=6 cols, round(10/3)+1=4 rows, not 4x3). Two increment clicks on the strip's own spacing stepper (data-field="spacing", added so this is reachable at all) raise it 3->5 before dragging, so the click reaches the exact grid the command names.

expect.note: 3 rows x 4 cols = 12, matching the command's declared pattern now that the click actually uses spacing:5

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:8 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:8 depth:6 start:20,20 BlastWorkshop auto-advances Drill -> Charge once holes exist, so re-using the grid tool needs an explicit click back to the Drill tab ([data-step="1"]) first. The spacing stepper also carries its value over from the first grid above (now 5, not the 3m default) — 3 more increments reach this step's declared spacing:8 (round(8/8)+1=2 cols/rows, matching rows:2 cols:2) before dragging. depth corrected from 10 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. Only holeCount is asserted here (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction.
